Nemencine Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vilniaus apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Jews likely began settling in Nemenčinė following the expulsion of Russian Jews from villages in May 1882; the population reached 340 by 1885. Rabbi Yaakov Halevi Kopstein became the community's rabbi in 1884 and served for almost half a century. Community life, disrupted by WWI-era violence, was restored in 1920 with help from the JDC and YEKOPO; Nemenčinė natives who had emigrated to the US funded the construction of a new beit-midrash. On September 20, 1941, following the German arrival that June, most of Nemenčinė's Jewish residents were murdered in the forest; a few escaped and joined the partisans.
